concerns.concern: The C2z symmetry argument is model-independent, so it applies equally to any voltage even in current, including gate-oscillation and heating artefacts. Nothing in the data shown separates these from boundary-mode transport.
concerns.quote: The same reasoning seems to apply to any voltage that is even in the current, including the gate and heating mechanisms above.

concerns.concern: Self-gating of the SrTiO3 back gate by the Hall and longitudinal voltages could produce the signal and is argued against but not tested. The source/drain ground swap does not remove position-dependent density modulation. The reviewer asks for a model calculation from the measured linear coefficients and gate capacitance, and for the second Hall pair to be measured.
concerns.quote: A ground swap leaves the position-dependent density modulation in place, so Extended Data Fig. 3 doesn't separate it.

concerns.concern: Second-harmonic signals from AC gate-voltage oscillation are excluded only by one ground swap, done at one gate voltage and at 1.7 K. The reviewer asks for the swap to be repeated at 25 mK and at other gate voltages, plus one-at-a-time Hall-electrode grounding.
concerns.quote: Source and drain ground swapped: part (one gate voltage, 1.7 K); Hall electrodes grounded one at a time: no

concerns.concern: Joule-heating thermoelectric voltages at 2ω are not separated from the claimed effect. The reviewer asks for an estimate of the temperature rise at 2 μA (25 mK) and 5 μA (1.7 K), and a comparison with a power-times-Nernst-like field shape.
concerns.quote: Thermoelectric part separated by its symmetry and field dependence: no; Control where heating remains and the claimed mechanism is absent: no

concerns.concern: The Hall bars' C2z symmetry is only approximate. Contact resistances of the pressed indium contacts and the shape and contact symmetry of the scratched Hall bars are not reported.
concerns.quote: What are the resistances of the pressed indium contacts, and how symmetric are the scratched Hall bars in shape and contact placement?

concerns.concern: The paper does not say how many of the devices (S1–S4, or Hall bars in total) show the opposite-sign second-harmonic voltages. It also does not explain why S1 is featured or why S3 and S4 were measured only in the PPMS.
concerns.quote: The paper doesn't say how many of the four show the effect, or why S1 leads.

concerns.concern: Other devices are not shown under the main-text conditions. S3 and S4 should be shown at the Fig. 2 gate voltages, and the second-best device at 25 mK, since S2 appears only at two gate voltages and 1 μA.
concerns.quote: State how many of S1 to S4 show the sign-reversed pair, and put S3 and S4 at the gate voltages of Fig. 2 into the PDF

concerns.concern: The choice of the five gate voltages and of 2 μA at 25 mK is not justified beyond a heating remark. The paper also does not report what other ranges were measured: other currents, gate voltages, cooldowns, or tilted field.
concerns.quote: The reasons for the five field-sweep gate voltages in Fig. 2, and for 2 μA at 25 mK, go no further than the heating remark on p. 6.

concerns.concern: Processing is underspecified. The paper does not say how hysteretic up/down branches were paired in the field antisymmetrization or which lock-in phase was used. Raw left and right voltages behind Fig. 1e are not shown.
concerns.quote: The paper doesn't say how the hysteretic branches are paired, which lock-in phase is used

concerns.concern: The code for the nonlinear Landauer-Büttiker simulations is not made available.
concerns.quote: or where the simulation code is.
